small_guidance:
- The current kernel still calls `torch.nn.Conv3d` (PyTorch) before launching the fused post-conv kernel — the conv is the heavy op and dominates runtime. Tuning `BLOCK_S`/`num_warps` on the elementwise+GN+mean tail will yield marginal gains; try `BLOCK_S=1024`, `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=2` only as a stopgap.
- The two-pass design recomputes hardswish; for the tail kernel, consider a single-pass Welford reduction fused with the affine+mean to halve memory reads of `x_flat`.
- Ensure `x_flat` skips the `.contiguous()` copy when conv output already is contiguous (it is, after reshape on a contiguous tensor) — avoid the reshape allocation by passing the 5D tensor directly with computed strides.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton conv3d kernel: implement as an implicit-im2col GEMM with one program per `(B, OC_tile, output-spatial tile)`. With OC=16, KD=KH=KW=4, IC=3 → K = 3·64 = 192, and output spatial = 13·29·29 = 10933 per batch; tile (BLOCK_M=16 over OC, BLOCK_N=64 or 128 over spatial, BLOCK_K=32 or full 192). Fuse the conv bias add, HardSwish, and even the GroupNorm pass-1 (sum/sumsq) into the epilogue so the conv output is never written to HBM just to be reread.
- Better: persistently keep the conv output for one `(B, group)` in registers/SMEM — emit per-program the partial sum/sumsq across the spatial tile, then a second small kernel (or atomics) finalizes mean/rstd and the affine+mean reduction. This removes the entire `x_flat` materialization (B·C·S = 1024·16·10933 fp32 ≈ 700 MB of traffic).
- Use channels_last3d (NDHWC) layout for the conv so the IC-axis loads coalesce across the GEMM-K dimension; weight should be pre-permuted to (OC, KD, KH, KW, IC) at init.
